category.title: Probability & Randomized Algorithms
category.description: Probability theory, Linearity of Expectation, Randomized QuickSort/QuickSelect, Monte Carlo, and Las Vegas algorithms.

algorithms.title: Linearity of Expectation & Probability
algorithms.summary: Computes expected value using property E[X1 + X2 + ... + Xn] = E[X1] + E[X2] + ... + E[Xn] regardless of independence.
explanation: 1. Fundamental Rule: `E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y]` holds EVEN IF variables X and Y are dependent!
2. Indicator Variables: Define `I_i` as binary indicator variable (1 if event `i` occurs, 0 otherwise). `E[I_i] = P(Event i)`.
3. Summing Indicators: Total Expected Count `E[X] = sum(P(Event i))`.

exampleTrace.title: Trace Expected Matches (Hat Check Problem for N people)
traceSteps: Person i gets their own hat with probability P(I_i = 1) = 1/N.
Result: Exactly 1 person gets their own hat on average!

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Computes expected average outcomes in complex probabilistic processes.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding expected number of steps, matches, or trials.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Randomized algorithm analysis, gaming drop rate expectations, financial risk metrics.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Splits complex joint probability distribution into simple linear expectation sums.

algorithms.title: Randomized QuickSort & QuickSelect
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(N log N) Expected QuickSort / O(N) Expected QuickSelect
algorithms.summary: Picks pivot elements uniformly at random to guarantee expected O(N log N) sorting and O(N) K-th element selection.
explanation: 1. Deterministic Worst Case: Fixed pivot (e.g. first element) degrades to O(N^2) on sorted arrays.
2. Random Pivot Strategy: Pick `pivot_idx = random(low, high)`. Swap `arr[pivot_idx]` with `arr[high]`.
3. Expected O(N log N): Randomized pivot guarantees balanced partitions with high probability, destroying malicious adversarial inputs.

exampleTrace.title: Trace QuickSelect for 2nd smallest in [7, 10, 4, 3, 20, 15]
traceSteps: Partition array around 7: Left=[4, 3], Pivot=7, Right=[10, 20, 15].
Pivot index is 2 -> Target K=2 found!

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Eliminates O(N^2) worst-case performance spikes caused by structured inputs.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When sorting or finding K-th order statistic reliably in real systems.
wAnswers.whereUsed: C++ `std::nth_element`, operating system process priority schedulers.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Guarantees linear expected time O(N) for K-th smallest element.

algorithms.title: Monte Carlo vs Las Vegas Algorithms
algorithms.summary: Distinguishes Monte Carlo (fixed runtime, probabilistic output correctness like Miller-Rabin) from Las Vegas (probabilistic runtime, guaranteed correct output like QuickSelect).
explanation: 1. Las Vegas Algorithms: Always return correct answer. Runtime is a random variable (e.g. Randomized QuickSort, Randomized QuickSelect).
2. Monte Carlo Algorithms: Fixed deterministic runtime. Output has a small probability of error `P(error) <= 1/4^k` (e.g. Miller-Rabin Primality Test, Karger's Min-Cut).
3. Error Reduction: Running a Monte Carlo algorithm K times exponentially reduces error probability to `(1/4)^K`.

exampleTrace.title: Trace Miller-Rabin Primality (Monte Carlo) on N = 561
traceSteps: 561 is Carmichael number (pseudo-prime for Fermat test).
Miller-Rabin picks random base a=2 -> detects non-trivial square root of 1 mod 561.
Correctly flags 561 as COMPOSITE in O(k log^3 N) deterministic time.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Solves computationally intractable problems using probabilistic random sampling.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When exact deterministic algorithms are too slow (e.g. primality testing for 1024-bit numbers).
wAnswers.whereUsed: RSA keygen Miller-Rabin test, Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) in AlphaGo.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Achieves sub-exponential time bounds with arbitrarily low error probability.

import random

def miller_rabin(n: int, k: int = 5) -> bool:
    if n <= 1 or n == 4: return False
    if n <= 3: return True
    d = n - 1
    s = 0
    while d % 2 == 0:
        d //= 2
        s += 1
    for _ in range(k):
        a = random.randint(2, n - 2)
        x = pow(a, d, n)
        if x == 1 or x == n - 1: continue
        for _ in range(s - 1):
            x = (x * x) % n
            if x == n - 1: break
        else:
            return False
    return True
